messages.author: b0084e74319ebcb3
messages.subject: Site covariates vs 'point' covariates
parts:
Hello all,
I have point count data and I am fitting models using distsamp to evaluate how continuous variables affect abundance (e.g. canopy height, elevation). We recorded habitat variables per point on several localities, and I am entering these variables per point as site covariates (siteCovs) when constructing the unmarked data frame. But these are not really site covariates but 'point' or 'observation' covariates. But I am having second thoughts and I am not entirely sure if this could be wrong and one should use average conditions per site to make predictions about abundance. This would be problematic because conditions within site are very variable. I wanted to know your opinion on this subject so I appreciate any comments or reading suggestions (different that unmarked documentation). Thanks a lot in advance!
Best,
Laura

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Site covariates vs 'point' covariates
parts:
hi Laura,
 the model implemented in distsamp is a SITE-level model, using site level totals (per distance class) and therefore it requires site level covariate summaries. Thus if you have within-site covariates you must aggregate them up to the level of the site.
 It is possible to model within-site covariates (e.g., see chapter 9 of the AHM book), and we have a hacked function in unmarked called pcount.spHDS for that, but it requires a complete raster coverage of the covariate (not sampled)
 Also see this really great paper here
http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1365-2664.13053/full

messages.author: b0084e74319ebcb3
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Site covariates vs 'point' covariates
parts:
Hello all,
Thanks Marc and Jeffrey for your response and suggestions.
I was referring to point as each one of the points where we counted birds (point count), not the exact location where the animals were detected. With site I was referring to localities (we have several). In each locality we did between 10 and 30 points. Within each locality there was important variation in the habitat variables of interest (e.g. elevation and canopy height) so we recorded these at each point count. My question is, does each point count correspond to a 'site'? This is how I am interpreting it. Also, is it problematic to include point counts from multiple localities in the same model? Again, I really appreciate your comments and suggestions. Thank you!
Best,
Laura
